A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LABE/LAC study. Main text, appendices, all 26 tables, and all four figures are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original classifier evaluations, analyses of agency bias in human-written and LLM-generated texts, and prompt-based mitigation experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including classifier performance and detailed demographic comparisons in the appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same descriptor-based generation, LAC construction and annotation procedure, fine-tuned BERT agency classifier, and bias measurement pipeline. Revised explanations and relocated classifier details do not change the method.

E1.justification: The same three generation tasks, 5,400 prompts, binary-gender/four-race coverage, and 3,724-sentence LAC dataset are retained. Bias in Bios, RateMyProfessor, and the Wan et al. reference-letter proxy also remain unchanged in documented coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 12 and v4 Table 11 contain the same classifier comparisons: string matching, sentiment, Wan et al. (2023), Llama2 variants, BERT, and RoBERTa. The ChatGPT, Mistral, and Llama3 comparisons and mitigation conditions are also retained.

E3.justification: The LAC splits, biography sampling, professor-review filtering, classifier training budgets, model versions, generation settings, and evaluation metrics match. Moving dataset statistics into Appendix B.5 does not introduce a new protocol.

E4.justification: Profession- and department-stratified analyses, the illustrative agency-classification example, and mitigation amplification/overshooting analyses are retained. v4 Appendix D reorganizes existing results from v2 Appendix E.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over random seeds 0, 1, and 2 and the same annotation-agreement assessment. Neither adds repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: All matched numerical tables and figure graphics are unchanged. For example, v2 Table 4 and v4 Table 1 retain overall unmitigated bias scores of 34.40, 45.81, and 56.81 for ChatGPT, Mistral, and Llama3; classifier and appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The agency definitions and ratio-gap/variance reasoning remain unchanged. Section 3.3 rephrases the metrics' roles without introducing a new mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the explicit 'On most generation tasks' qualification from the claim that intersectional bias exceeds other bias dimensions, making that headline less qualified. The LABE/LAC contributions and four central conclusions otherwise remain the same.

C2.justification: Interpretations of demographic disparities and mitigation failures, the reference-letter proxy qualification, and applicability limitations are retained. The new Ethics Statement repeats safeguards already discussed in v2 Appendix G rather than adding a substantive qualification.

D1.justification: Section 4.1.1 replaces the RateMyProfessor GitHub access link with a Mendeley Data link. This changes access information without establishing an underlying dataset change; preprocessing, prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, and timing disclosures otherwise match.

R1.justification: v4 adds Field et al. (2022), Controlled analyses of social biases in Wikipedia bios, replacing unresolved citations. It removes bibliography entries for Aragón et al. (2023) and Field and Tsvetkov (2019), while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and several explanations are shortened, dataset statistics move to Appendix B.5, and classifier documentation is consolidated into Appendix B. Limitations move before the references, with a largely repetitive Ethics Statement added; the main narrative remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column presentation, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. The human-versus-LLM table moves to the appendix, and gender-result Tables 17–18 share a page in v4. These are substantial layout changes with unchanged visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Replacing unresolved citations with an identifiable Field et al. reference and making existing limitations prominent provide modest gains in traceability and transparency. The scientific evidence is unchanged. Repetitive ethics text and the less-qualified abstract wording limit, but do not outweigh, these editorial gains.
